investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every new agent pod was left unschedulable: the Kubernetes scheduler reported 2 nodes with Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes that did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0 of 6 nodes available. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the runner never obtained a VM ID or a remote state value, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent and the expected-output contract is entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The production Kubernetes cluster's kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is exhausted on the two nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) indicates those nodes have no remaining VM slots to allocate. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, so preemption cannot help. Because the pod never starts, the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885: createAgent called with machineType "remote") never reaches the point where it can write orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState into the evidence object, causing a total contract gap. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885, which is the call that triggers remote pod creation; it is never reached successfully.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated without a running pod.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all three eval checks hit the same scheduler error within a ~5-minute window, indicating the resource pool was already at capacity before any eval pod was submitted.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are also the only ones carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, leaving no fallback scheduling path.
QUATERNARY — Cluster-level VM quota or cloud provider limit on peer-pod VM instances reached, preventing the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource from being replenished even if existing pods were evicted.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity available on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different scheduling or API error would need to be investigated.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeded and produced all four required evidence fields, it would suggest a transient capacity spike rather than sustained exhaustion.
If the pod spec for remote agents did not request kata.peerpods.io/vm as a resource, the scheduler message would be unrelated to the eval runner's pod and the root cause would need to be re-examined.

If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed, a shared infrastructure capacity cause would be less likely and a check-specific runner bug would be more likely.
If the node affinity/selector matched more than 2 nodes, the 4-node mismatch count would change and the cluster topology assumption would need revision.

Add an eval that detects stuck or long-running remote-agent pods (e.g., pods in Pending or Running state beyond a TTL) and alerts before they exhaust the VM resource pool.

Add a pre-flight eval that verifies at least one node with the required affinity label has available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity before attempting remote agent creation, to distinguish capacity exhaustion from API or runner failures earlier in the check lifecycle.

Consider a dedicated eval for node affinity/selector coverage that confirms the expected number of nodes (currently 2) match the remote agent pod's scheduling requirements, alerting if that count drops to zero.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity — All Three remote-agents Checks Failing
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-25T16:39–16:44Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent was never created, and the remote-agent-state eval probe never reached the state-polling stage, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) completely absent.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota across the two nodes that carry that resource. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote agent pod submitted by the eval runner stalls as Unschedulable for ~140–145 seconds before the probe times out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM node pool; it is an eval-detected signal of a production infrastructure constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage (no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence).

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: the cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, and their combined capacity is fully consumed by existing workloads, leaving no room for the eval's probe pod. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, meaning the schedulable pool is artificially constrained to 2 nodes. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or a node label was removed, the effective capacity is smaller than the total cluster size.

QUATERNARY — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the two eligible nodes may be too small for concurrent eval runs plus live workloads, causing transient exhaustion even without leaks.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes swarm cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner never received any response evidence, leaving all five required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing remote agent provisioning has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class, and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod request times out unscheduled (~139–152 s across all three checks). This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no evidence of user-traffic or broader service impact is present in the packet.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every new agent pod was left unschedulable: the Kubernetes scheduler reported 2 nodes with Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes that did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0 of 6 nodes available. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the runner never obtained a VM ID or a remote state value, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent and the expected-output contract is entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The production Kubernetes cluster's kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is exhausted on the two nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) indicates those nodes have no remaining VM slots to allocate. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, so preemption cannot help. Because the pod never starts, the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885: createAgent called with machineType "remote") never reaches the point where it can write orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState into the evidence object, causing a total contract gap. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated without a running pod.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all three eval checks hit the same scheduler error within a ~5-minute window, indicating the resource pool was already at capacity before any eval pod was submitted.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are also the only ones carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, leaving no fallback scheduling path.
QUATERNARY — Cluster-level VM quota or cloud provider limit on peer-pod VM instances reached, preventing the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource from being replenished even if existing pods were evicted.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-25T16:39–16:44Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent was never created, and the remote-agent-state eval probe never reached the state-polling stage, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) completely absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota across the two nodes that carry that resource. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote agent pod submitted by the eval runner stalls as Unschedulable for ~140–145 seconds before the probe times out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM node pool; it is an eval-detected signal of a production infrastructure constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage (no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence).

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful remote-agent pod scheduling event on the same cluster at the same time would disprove that capacity was fully exhausted.

kubectl describe node output showing available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots remaining on the 2 affinity-matching nodes would indicate the root cause is a misconfigured resource request or quota limit rather than true exhaustion.
A passing run of remote-agent-create or remote-agent-runtime in the same production-api environment shortly after this failure would suggest a transient spike rather than sustained exhaustion.
Evidence that the pod's node affinity/selector was recently changed to target a smaller or different node pool would shift the root cause toward a configuration drift rather than capacity exhaustion.
Cluster autoscaler logs showing a scale-up event that succeeded would indicate the issue was transient and self-healing.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that directly checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on each eligible node and fails with a warning before slots reach zero, providing earlier signal before pod scheduling fails.
Add an eval that detects remote-agent pods stuck in Pending or Terminating state for longer than a configurable threshold, catching leaked VMs before they exhaust scheduling capacity.
Add a cluster node-pool health eval that verifies the count of nodes matching the remote-agent affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold, catching node pool shrinkage or affinity drift.
Consider a canary eval that attempts a remote-agent pod dry-run scheduling check (without actually starting the VM) to validate schedulability without consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots.
